newsitem.title: USA: Multimedia Games to implement changes.
newsitem.headline: Multimedia Games to implement changes.

text.p: Multimedia Games Inc said Thursday it signed a memorandum of understanding with the National Indian Gaming Commission to make certain changes to the company's high-speed video game, MegaMania, in order to maintain the commission's classification of the game as bingo.

Such classification allows MegaMania to be offered by high-stakes Indian bingo halls in all 47 of those states where charity bingo is allowed by state law as long as the game occurs on Indian trust land.

The changes were developed in response to an analysis by the commission, the Department of Justice and the U.S. attorney for the Northern District of Oklahoma, which began an investigation of this subject about a year ago.

"We are on a fast track to complete the changes and are pleased the government has granted us reasonable time to comply," said chief executive officer Gordon Graves. "Receipt of this letter closes a chapter of legal uncertainty that has clouded our status for the past nine months or more."
